item.title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.26718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.
item.dc:creator: Florian K\"onig, Marius Wiesemann, Giulia Zanderighi

item.title: Study of Radiative Muon Capture Experimental Data and its Implications for Muon-Conversion Experiments
item.description: arXiv:2611.26817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. We develop a model characterized by distinct nucleon-knockout final states, each with its associated multibody phase space and kinematic endpoint. This framework is applied to photon data from TRIUMF and positron data from SINDRUM II, and the results are compared to the previously used closure approximation. We find that separately modeling the distinct nucleon-knockout final states provides an improved description of the available RMC data near the endpoint, and we discuss the implications for the COMET and Mu2e experiments.
item.dc:creator: Yury Kolomensky, Michael MacKenzie, Ryan Plestid, Matthew Stortini, Ajla Trumic

item.title: Computing the Wave: Bridging Gravitational Wave and High-Energy-Physics software (with modular ROOT extensions)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-Energy Physics (HEP) and Gravitational Wave (GW) astronomy pursue different scientific goals, yet they face strikingly similar computing challenges and can enrich one another through shared software. Building on the prototype presented at ACAT 2024, we report on the consolidation of that work into a single, modular extension of the CERN ROOT data-analysis framework, freely distributed under RIOPlus. The library is now organised as a set of optional, dynamically loadable extensions covering configuration and file-format parsing (including the Gravitational Wave Frame (GWF) format and HDF5), remote and federated data access (OSDF/Pelican, S3, Kafka) with token-based credentials, an enhanced dynamic-display manager, an advanced signal-processing layer built on the KFR library, and a complex-capable tensor layer backed by LibTorch with ONNX interoperability. We summarise the design of each extension, outline the intended application to transient-noise (glitch) detection and classification, and update the FFT performance benchmark comparing KFR with FFTW. We close with the end-to-end ROOT-centred workflow these extensions enable, its current status, and an outlook toward column-wise RNTuple storage.
item.dc:creator: Marco Meyer-Conde (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific, Virgo,KAGRA Collaborations), Hirotaka Takahashi (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific, Virgo,KAGRA Collaborations), Nobuyuki Kanda (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific, Virgo,KAGRA Collaborations), Ken-ichi Oohara (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific, Virgo,KAGRA Collaborations), Kazuki Sakai (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific, Virgo,KAGRA Collaborations)

item.title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. We then propose two targeted approaches to repair the flaw: by removing three latent directions identified with sparse autoencoders, and by letting language-model agents edit the weights directly, without gradients and with only 50 queries to the model. Both their edits individually remove almost the entire flaw and leave the rest of the model's response nearly unchanged. Compared to fine-tuning, both methods change far fewer parameters. Although built only on $W$ and QCD jets, the edits carry over to all signal classes, the pretrained generator, and a newly trained regression head.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Bonnet-Guerrini, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, Troels Petersen

item.title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data. Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma] = 0.57\) and \(\Gamma(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\). By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component. In addition, we also obtain \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state. More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.
item.dc:creator: Shirui Zhao, Yuxuan Du, Manying Pan, Hongxia Huang, Jialun Ping

item.title: nuSTORM: a unique GeV electron-(anti)neutrino machine
item.description: arXiv:2611.27549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this conference contribution, I briefly review current experimental programmes measuring the Dirac CP phase {\delta}CP using accelerator neutrinos. I argue that the nuSTORM concept---neutrino beams from a muon storage ring---could provide high-quality electron-(anti)neutrino beams needed for the cross-section inputs to {\delta}CP measurements.
item.dc:creator: Xianguo Lu

item.title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
item.description: arXiv:2611.27602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.
item.dc:creator: Waqas Ahmed, George K. Leontaris

item.title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
item.description: arXiv:2611.27636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.
item.dc:creator: Anne-Mazarine Lyon, Etiennette Auffray, Marco Caporale, Katerina Decka, Michael Doser, Jean-Louis Faure, Greta Gajdan, Yacine Haddad, Jan Kral, Joseph Mariano, Loris Martinazzoli, Emanuele Mazzola, Eva Mihokova, Solangel Rojas Torres, Matteo Salomoni, Vojtech Zabloudil

item.title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state. In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator. Starting from perturbatively produced ($c\overline{c}$) and ($b\overline{b}$) pairs, we examine how the formation of heavy-flavour mesons and baryons, including $D^0$, $B^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, and $\Lambda_b^0$, is accompanied by compensating particles elsewhere. The analysis focuses on correlations between the identified heavy hadron and the hadronic system responsible for balancing its conserved quantum numbers. We compare three hadronisation configurations that are implemented in PYTHIA: the Monash tune, colour-reconnection models incorporating string junctions (SJ), and close-packing (CP) approaches. We find that the SJ and CP tunes show a substantially enhanced contribution of baryons to the charm and beauty balancing yields compared with the Monash tune; this enhancement becomes more pronounced in high-multiplicity events. This study introduces a framework for characterising quantum-number compensation in heavy-flavour production and provides a new way to test hadronisation dynamics using identified charm- and beauty-hadron correlations, which can be explored at current and future collider experiments.
item.dc:creator: I\~naki Pardo Zambrana, Paul Veen, K. Keri Vos, Panos Christakoglou

item.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
item.description:
arXiv:2611.27985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($\delta$) is 0 or $\pi$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $
u_\mu$ and $
u_	au$, but not the $
u_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sin\delta$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sin\delta$ dependence to be probed in $
u_\mu$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $
u_\mu$ survival probability.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Barenboim, Stephen J. Parke, Alberto S\'anchez Vargas

item.title: Cross sections of $\eta$ mesons in $p$$+$$p$ collisions at forward rapidity at $\sqrt{s}=500$ GeV and central rapidity at $\sqrt{s}=510$ GeV
item.description: arXiv:2507.04896v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first measurements of the forward and midrapidity $\eta$-meson cross sections from $p$$+$$p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=500$ and $510$~GeV, respectively. We also report the midrapidity $\eta/\pi^0$ ratio at 510 GeV. The forward cross section is measured differentially in $\eta$-meson transverse momentum ($p_T$) from 1.0 to 6.5~GeV/$c$ for pseudorapidity $3.0<|\eta|<3.8$. The midrapidity cross section is measured from 3.5 to 44 GeV/$c$ for pseudorapidity $|\eta|<0.35$. Both cross sections serve as critical inputs to an updated global analysis of the $\eta$-meson fragmentation functions.

item.title: First Measurement of Sub-GeV $\nu_{\mu}$ Charged-Current Coherent Pion Production on Argon in MicroBooNE
item.description: arXiv:2606.13613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a measurement of the charged-current coherent pion production cross section on argon using the MicroBooNE liquid argon time projection chamber exposed to the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab. The measurement uses the MicroBooNE data set corresponding to $1.26 \times 10^{21}$ protons on target with a mean neutrino energy of $0.8$~GeV. The flux-averaged cross section is measured to be $(9.1 \pm 1.2_{\text{stat}} \pm 1.2_\text{syst}) \times 10^{-40}\,\text{cm}^2/\text{Ar}$. This result represents the first measurement of charged-current coherent pion production on argon at sub-GeV neutrino energies. Due to its clean two-body kinematics, where the neutrino interacts coherently with the entire nucleus producing a forward muon and pion with no nuclear breakup, this process provides a useful tool for constraining neutrino flux uncertainties in current and future oscillation experiments such as DUNE.

item.title: Real-time lepton identification at LHCb in Run 3 using Lipschitz neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.07903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The LHCb physics program in Run 3 relies critically on the efficient real-time selection of events containing muons and electrons, which are key signatures in a wide range of heavy-flavor and exotic decay processes. The LHCb Run 3 detector now operates with a fully software-based trigger that processes the complete detector readout at the LHC bunch-crossing rate, with the first trigger stage executed on GPUs. In this environment, particle-identification algorithms must achieve high efficiency and background rejection while satisfying stringent constraints on throughput and memory footprint. We present algorithms for muon and electron identification in the LHCb Run 3 GPU trigger based on Lipschitz-constrained neural networks. Separate networks are developed for muons and electrons and are trained using simulated events. Their performance is evaluated relative to the previous baseline algorithms, demonstrating improved discrimination across a wide range of kinematic regions while remaining compatible with the requirements of real-time GPU execution.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Casais Vidal, Kate A. Richardson, Maarten Van Veghel, Marco Santimaria, Marianna Fontana, Mike Williams

item.title: Density-Guided Conditional Neural Processes for Detector Efficiency Estimation
item.description:
arXiv:2609.13593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Searches for rare events such as neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0
u eta eta$) and dark matter infer a physical rate from a handful of events. The efficiency of the event selection is therefore critical, as it directly impacts the sensitivity of the search. In germanium detectors, a pulse-shape selection keeps single-site events, which resemble the $0
u eta eta$ signal, and rejects multi-site gamma-ray backgrounds. Its efficiency is measured with calibration data and changes sharply at spectral peaks, where the fraction of single-site events changes. With limited calibration data, a smooth estimator erases these changes, while a flexible one mistakes statistical fluctuations for physical structure. To resolve this tension, we introduce a density-guided conditional neural process (CNP) that permits rapid variation only at energies where calibration events concentrate. On public MAJORANA calibration data, it recovers the double-escape peak, the reference for the $0
u eta eta$ signal, and it remains smooth in the continuum around the $0
u eta eta$ energy. With half as many training events, it outperforms CNP and Attentive CNP baselines both at the peaks and in the continuum. This reduction opens the way to continuous monitoring of the efficiency of individual detectors in ton-scale $0
u eta eta$ experiments such as LEGEND-1000.
item.dc:creator: Yue Ma, Aobo Li

item.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays
item.description: arXiv:2609.17726v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing the mass of a heavy resonance from its decay products with missing energy is one of the central tasks that directly determine the sensitivity in new physics searches at collider experiments. Supervised learning approaches to this problem often struggle to generalize well due to the presence of various systematic uncertainties and distribution shifts. Exhausting all possible variations in the labeled data can be very compute-intensive, while a failure of the model to generalize can corrupt the reconstructed resonance widths that are critical in peak-hunting analyses. In this work, following the foundation model paradigm, we use a self-supervised approach to pre-train a transformer encoder with VICReg to learn an embedding invariant to various corruptions, then fine-tune it for mass regression on a heavy resonance with masses ranging from 2.5 to 6.5 TeV and a SUSY-like cascade decay into an eleven-body final state. We show that the pre-trained model reconstructs sharper resonance peaks and has a more stable performance under various realistic corruptions, compared to a supervised model of the same architecture trained on the same augmented data from scratch.
item.dc:creator: Ho Fung Tsoi, Alex Yang, Luis Felipe Gutierrez Zagazeta, Shion Chen, Dylan Sheldon Rankin

item.title: Similarity Pairing with Energy Mover's Distance for Self-Supervised Pre-Training at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2609.17738v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many self-supervised methods for training foundation models at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) rely on data augmentations to encourage the model to embed events into a representation space invariant to certain physical or detector symmetries. A common challenge arises from the large freedom in choosing a proper set of augmentations on which downstream performance depends. The implementation of augmentations involves either modifying existing events, potentially breaking the event fidelity, or simulating more event variants, which is computationally intensive. In this work, we present a data-driven method of pairing events by their similarity via the energy mover's distance (EMD), which measures how similar two events are in terms of the work required to transform one into the other. With this approach, distinct events are sampled and matched by their similarity to serve as views for learning invariance, keeping the physics content of each event intact without handcrafted distortions. We demonstrate this augmentation-free pairing method by pre-training on QCD jets via self-distillation and show that it can yield semantic jet embeddings with downstream discrimination power comparable to or better than an augmentation-based baseline.
item.dc:creator: Ho Fung Tsoi, Dylan Sheldon Rankin

item.title: Probing Dark Matter Interactions with Stellar Motion near Sagittarius A*
item.description: arXiv:2510.07387v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stars orbiting Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) at the Milky Way's center provide a unique laboratory to test gravity and dark matter (DM). We demonstrate that DM interactions in stellar interiors induce a novel momentum transfer force, altering orbits beyond gravitational effects. We derive the first astrophysical constraints on DM-nucleon scattering using S2's 2000-2019 orbital data probing sub-GeV parameter space for specified DM distributions near Sgr A*. We further show that complementary orbital survival constraints and future observations of highly eccentric S-stars extend the reach to DM profiles allowed by present gravitational measurements. Unlike bounds requiring DM capture and annihilation, our constraints apply broadly to scattering DM including asymmetric DM, and extend to masses where methods based on capture can lose sensitivity. Stellar lifetime constraints over Myr timescales complement these, surpassing some direct detection and cosmological limits. This work establishes stellar dynamics as a novel probe of DM interactions.
item.dc:creator: R. Andrew Gustafson, Ian M. Shoemaker, Volodymyr Takhistov

item.title: Two-Dimensional Transverse-Momentum Subtraction and Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering at N$^3$LO in QCD
item.description: arXiv:2603.29673v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Identified hadron production is essential for the study of nucleon structure and QCD hadronization at high energies. We present the first calculation of unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in perturbative QCD. Our calculation is based on a novel method of two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction motivated by QCD factorization of soft and collinear singularities. The N$^3$LO corrections are moderate in general but can be significant in threshold regions, and exhibit excellent perturbative convergence and reduced scale variations. The fully differential framework allows for arbitrary selection cuts and directly enables precision nucleon tomography at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider, establishing the theory foundation needed to match the anticipated experimental accuracy. Generalization of the method to calculations of polarized SIDIS is also feasible.
item.dc:creator: Liang Dong, Shen Fang, Jun Gao, Hai Tao Li, Ding Yu Shao, Hua Xing Zhu, Yu Jiao Zhu

item.title: Inpainting to search for premerger massive black hole binaries in realistic LISA datasets
item.description: arXiv:2605.13738v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A key science target of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is to carry out multi-messenger observations of massive black hole binaries, observing the merger simultaneously in gravitational waves and with electromagnetic observatories. Identifying that a merger is happening and providing an updating estimate of the sky location in the hours, days and weeks before the merger is critical to enable electromagnetic observations of the merger event. In this work we demonstrate and compare two methods for premerger identification of massive black hole binaries; a zero-latency filter approach and, for the first time, an approach using an ``inpainting'' technique. We apply these methods to the LISA Data Challenge dataset 2a--Sangria-HM--and demonstrate the successful recovery of the 14 signals in the dataset that we expected to be identifiable at least half a day before merger. We show that the inpainting method can identify premerger signals even when gaps are present in the data, demonstrating the recovery of a signal even when 3 day-long data gaps are added to the 14 days preceding merger. Finally, we explore the challenge of overlapping signals, using a region of overlapping signals in the Sangria-HM dataset, all of which merge within a 10-day window, and show how removing signals that have been confidently identified from the data allows us to identify quieter signals in the same period.
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cabourn Davies, Ian Harry

item.title: Impact of Environmental Stress on Low Gain Avalanche Diode Sensors Response
item.description: arXiv:2608.22482v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low Gain Avalanche Diodes or LGADs are silicon sensors capable of achieving excellent timing resolution due to their characteristic internal gain. Detectors based on LGAD technology play a crucial role in High Energy and Nuclear Physics experiments, among other applications. However, their performance is affected by environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and storage conditions. A systematic evaluation of the response of LGAD sensors as a function of these environmental parameters is therefore of essential importance for any application. LGAD sensors fabricated at the Brookhaven National Laboratory are characterized and stress-tested against various operating conditions, such as rapid temperature and humidity changes. Dedicated and detailed simulations are used to interpret the experimental results.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Hijas Mohamed Farook, Gaetano Barone, Diallo Boye, Gabriele D'Amen, Gabriele Giacomini, Timo Peltola, Jennifer Roloff, Enrico Rossi, Trevor Russell, Sally Seidel, Alessandro Tricoli, Lixing Wang
